scope: Comparison research only; no marketplace specimen added for ShortSync, Twitch, TikTok or Instagram.

vendor_posting_snapshot.selection: Creators using a cross-posting service, disproportionately multiplatform, not a random sample
vendor_posting_snapshot.denominator_warning: Platform share is share of posts; pair shares are among 50,175 multi-platform uploads; an upload generates one or more successful post events.
vendor_posting_snapshot.license: CC BY 4.0 for published aggregate figures

historical_competition_paper.event: Twitch Prime exposure increase after Amazon Prime bundling
historical_competition_paper.population: studied YouTube and Twitch content creators single-homing versus multihoming; historical competitive shock
historical_competition_paper.design: quasi-experimental difference in observed relative creator responses; theoretical game model
historical_competition_paper.publisher_conclusion: After exposure increased, sampled multihomers reduced effort and underperformed relative to single-homers
historical_competition_paper.notes: Not evidence every channel should single-home; channel incentives and competitive context differ.

decision_protocol: Export legally eligible owned assets independently from audiences, followers, watch histories and platform recommendations.
Measure creator publication effort, original vs cross-posted videos, rights and device-specific content compatibility.
Use opt-in first-party links or legitimately reported aggregate referral categories; never infer a cross-platform journey from reused hashtags or similar profile names.
Preregister target destination, identical time units, creator cohorts, acceptable cost and actual net receipts.
Account for simultaneous posting and selection into a cross-posting tool; no causal uplift without an appropriate counterfactual.
Do not pool the 2016 Twitch Prime event with October 2026 ShortSync publishing logs as if they measured one audience.
